title: Wile E. Coyote Finally Gets His Day in Court — and You Can Watch It at Home
summary:
Imagine working on a big movie for years — and then the studio locks it in a vault. That almost happened to Coyote vs. Acme, a Looney Tunes film starring everyone's favorite unlucky coyote. Warner Bros. decided not to release it. But another company, Ketchup Entertainment, swooped in and saved it. The movie hit theaters, and now you can watch it at home starting September 29, 2026. You can rent or buy it on Fandango, Prime Video, and Apple.

So what's it about? Wile E. Coyote is fed up. For decades, Acme Corporation has sold him gadgets that explode in his face instead of catching the Road Runner. So he does something wild: he takes Acme to court. The movie mixes cartoons with real actors, kind of like Who Framed Roger Rabbit. It's a David vs. Goliath story — a small guy taking on a giant company. Director Dave Green says it's funny, zany, and even a little touching. As the Road Runner would say: "Beep beep!"
why_it_matters: It is a fun reminder that even a small character can stand up to a giant company, and that when fans speak up loudly, something good can sometimes be saved.

background_read: Wile E. Coyote is a cartoon character from Looney Tunes, a set of funny cartoons made by Warner Bros. (a huge Hollywood movie company) since the 1930s.
In the cartoons, Acme Corporation is a made-up company that sells wild gadgets — and they always backfire on the coyote.
Movies sometimes get finished and then locked away. Warner Bros. also cancelled a nearly finished Batgirl movie a few years ago, so fans worried the coyote movie would never be seen.
Article_Structure: WHO: Wile E. Coyote stars in Coyote vs. Acme, a Looney Tunes movie that Warner Bros. decided not to release and Ketchup Entertainment rescued; director Dave Green made it.
WHAT: The film hit theaters, and from September 29, 2026 people can rent or buy it at home on Fandango, Prime Video and Apple.
WHERE: It is a Hollywood movie you can now watch at home, and the story itself happens in court, where the coyote sues Acme Corporation.
WHY: Acme's gadgets keep exploding in the coyote's face instead of catching the Road Runner, so he finally takes the giant company to court — a David vs. Goliath story.

perspectives.description: They are thrilled that a movie they thought they would never see got rescued and released.
Studios make very expensive movies, so some people argue a company has the right to decide what it does or does not release.
Finished movies do get cancelled or shelved more often than people realise, usually quietly and for money reasons.
